name: Liberal feminism
summary: Liberal feminism seeks equality between women and men through legal and political reform within liberal democracy, treating the denial of equal rights, education and economic opportunity as the main barrier. It works through legislatures, courts and enforcement of anti-discrimination law, aims to integrate women into the mainstream of public life, and welcomes men as partners. Its economics range from center-right to center-left.
scope: The mainstream liberal feminist tradition from Wollstonecraft and John Stuart Mill's Subjection of Women to the 1966 NOW Statement of Purpose (Friedan, Murray) and modern liberal feminist political philosophy (Okin, Nussbaum). It excludes radical, socialist and Marxist feminism, and libertarian and neoliberal variants are treated as strands. Many non-gender statements are inferred from center-left liberal democracy and given low confidence.

sources.title: The Subjection of Women
sources.author: John Stuart Mill

sources.title: National Organization for Women, Statement of Purpose (1966)
sources.author: NOW (Friedan and Murray)
sources.usedFor: Program of enforcing equal rights, childcare and retraining, equal education, and partnership with men.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a defining issue, but NOW-style liberal feminism backs public provision of services such as childcare and reproductive care and sits center-left on material inequality.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Women are over-represented in low-paid work, and the NOW statement cites the pay gap, so mainstream liberal feminists generally back wage floors; the sources do not name a figure.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Liberal feminism spans center-right to center-left on economics, so adherents are split; the mainstream treats the state as a needed enforcer of equal treatment rather than trusting markets alone.

public-ownership.rationale: Liberal feminism works within existing capitalist liberal democracy and does not call for public ownership of industry; this is left to socialist feminists.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Social-democratic strands support measures to reduce material inequality, though the neoliberal strand does not; the mainstream leans mildly in favour.

unions-good.rationale: NOW's statement calls for opening unions to women and challenging discrimination within them, treating unions as institutions to integrate rather than reject, and the mainstream is union-friendly.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mill and early liberal feminists prized married women's property rights, but the sources give no view on property as a near-absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Liberal feminists want legal duties on employers against sex discrimination, but general corporate regulation is not a core concern, so the answer is a mild yes.

cut-welfare.rationale: NOW opposes policies that foster dependence yet wants childcare and retraining programs; adherents do not generally favour cutting welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership belongs to socialist feminism; liberal feminism seeks integration into the existing economy.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the rights-based liberal framework, which resists trading civil liberties for security.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No stated position; the individual-autonomy emphasis pulls toward yes while the center-left mainstream is cautious, so adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Liberal feminists are divided between free-speech liberalism and anti-discrimination protections; the sources state no common position.

strong-leader.rationale: Liberal feminism pursues reform through law, legislatures and rights within liberal democracy, which is at odds with leaders bypassing constraints.

state-harmful.rationale: Liberal feminism relies on the state and law to end discrimination and is associated with state feminism; the NOW statement demands federal enforcement.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mainstream liberal feminist organisations in the US generally favour gun limits, but this is inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not a liberal feminist theme; inferred from center-left rights liberalism, though adherents also want enforcement of laws on violence against women.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Liberal feminists are divided: autonomy arguments favour legalisation, while NOW generally opposes prostitution though divided on how to approach it.

decide-locally.rationale: NOW seeks national enforcement of equal rights through the Constitution and federal law, so adherents lean towards national standards over local discretion.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from reformist, rights-based liberalism that favours rehabilitation over pure punishment.

traditional-family.rationale: NOW wants new institutions so that women need not be defined by child-rearing, and Mill attacks the legal authority of the husband; adherents reject the traditional family as society's foundation without disparaging family life.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Liberal feminism treats LGBT rights as a core issue in the 21st century and extends equal civil rights to all.

abortion-legal.rationale: Freer access to abortion is a listed priority of NOW and liberal feminism, framed through privacy and women's autonomy.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not a stated aim; liberal feminism's secular rights framework and history of challenging churches as discriminating institutions point to a mild no.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Liberal feminists back affirmative action and take an intersectional approach today; NOW's statement stresses that human rights are indivisible.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Mill argued that what is called women's nature is an eminently artificial thing shaped by circumstances, which liberal feminism inherits; adherents stop short of denying all innate difference.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not a feminist concern; liberal feminists generally put universal individual rights ahead of custom, which Mill calls weak evidence of merit.

gradual-change.rationale: Liberal feminism favours gradual reform through institutions over revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from universalist human-rights liberalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not a defining issue; rights-based liberalism and later liberal feminist engagement with UN gender-equality instruments suggest mild support, but this is inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Neoliberal and social-democratic strands differ on markets, and the sources say nothing on trade.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; liberal feminists are divided between human-rights interventionism and scepticism.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream liberals back generous immigration but not abolition of borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; mainstream liberal feminism is pro-growth and focused on integration into the economy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; adherents sit center-left, where climate action is supported, so this is a weak inference.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No stated view; liberal feminism neither affirms nor rejects technological optimism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed and not a gendered issue; adherents are split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Liberal feminism favours gradual reform within liberal democracy, in contrast to radical and socialist feminists.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses women's participation in the decision-making mainstream, which favours democratic over expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Liberal feminism accepts existing market economies and gives no support to planning, which Marxist feminists rather than liberal ones advance.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; the sources do not tie liberal feminism to any particular ownership form.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed and no stated view.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Mill's liberalism accepted limited inheritance taxation, but adherents have no common position.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; some feminists back it for care work, others fear it entrenches gender roles, so adherents split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal economic leanings.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from acceptance of market economies with a regulatory state.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed and no stated view.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Abolishing wage labor is a Marxist feminist demand; liberal feminism seeks women's equal access to paid work.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; no part of the mainstream tradition supports this.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from individual-rights liberalism.

one-party-rule.rationale: Liberal feminism operates within liberal democracy and pluralist political participation.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Mill attacks inherited, unchosen authority; adherents are mildly opposed though constitutional monarchy is not at issue.

democracy-best.rationale: Winning equal political rights and a place in the decision-making mainstream is central, and suffrage is a founding aim.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; no stated view on referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: A socialist institution that liberal feminism does not advance; it works through parliaments and courts.

right-to-secede.rationale: The sources record no liberal feminist stance on secession, and adherents hold no common view on it, so it is left neutral.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mill argued that male authority came from force and custom, and that natural fitness cannot be known when circumstances restrict women; liberal feminism rejects ascribed fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not directly addressed; reformist and pro-legal change means adherents mostly reject violence, though not absolutely.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; liberal and humanitarian commitments imply rejection.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not a stated demand, but liberal feminism challenges discrimination in churches and rests on secular rights; mild agreement.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Liberal feminism grounds rights in equal individual autonomy, not scripture, and challenges religious justifications of women's subordination.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Liberal feminism depends on public enforcement of equal rights, which libertarian privatisation would remove.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from center-left liberal leanings.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Universal human rights and the indivisibility of rights, as NOW states, are at odds with an ethnically defined nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Marxist reading of class conflict is rejected; liberal feminism seeks equality within existing society and welcomes cross-class coalitions.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Liberal feminism focuses on equality of opportunity and removal of legal barriers, though some strands support measures against material inequality.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Liberal feminism's sources never discuss reparations to colonised nations, and adherents differ on the question, so neutral.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Liberal feminism is individualistic, yet neoliberal and social-democratic strands differ and the sources do not endorse self-interest as a moral doctrine.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Liberal feminism is a rights-based doctrine in which equal individual rights come first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental value theory is outside liberal feminism's documented concerns, and adherents hold no shared position on it.

limit-population.rationale: Liberal feminists back voluntary reproductive choice, which implies rejecting active state limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; liberal feminism seeks women's integration into industrial society.

accelerate-technology.rationale: No source ties liberal feminism to speeding up technological disruption, and its reformist temperament neither endorses nor rejects it.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; autonomy arguments pull yes, caution pulls no.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from participation and rights commitments.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy appears nowhere in the liberal feminist sources, and adherents divide between privacy and safety arguments.

restore-past-order.rationale: Liberal feminism aims to overturn historical legal subordination of women and does not prize a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No stated position; the pragmatic style of liberal feminism pulls yes while principled rights claims pull no.

direct-action.rationale: Liberal feminism works through law, lobbying and elections more than direct action, which radical feminists favour.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources give no view on prefigurative politics; liberal feminists use conventional institutions without insisting methods mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from integration into modern society.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Liberal feminists want sexual division of labor removed by choice, not abolition of the division of labor in general.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Mill and NOW stress opportunity and equal pay for work, not distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed; a Marxist formulation outside the liberal feminist programme.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Marxist theory of exploitation belongs to socialist feminism, which liberal feminism is contrasted with.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Incompatible with liberal democracy and gradual reform.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist claim not held by liberal feminism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Liberal feminism asks for state action and funded programmes such as childcare; the libertarian claim is rejected by mainstream adherents.

harm-principle.rationale: Mill, the harm principle's author, is a founding liberal feminist; adherents back it broadly while some accept limits on harmful speech or exploitation.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Liberal feminism is individualistic and treats women as individuals with rights, though group-based anti-discrimination law is accepted.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; NOW-era feminists debated women's draft liability, and rights-liberalism leans against compulsion.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Political voice and the vote are central to the liberal feminist programme.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from belief in citizenship and rights rather than consumer exit.

positive-liberty.rationale: Liberal feminism backs childcare, retraining and equal-opportunity enforcement so women can act on their freedom, and social-democratic strands support material measures.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not stated; NOW protested false images of women in the media but did not claim media rule over elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Liberal feminism rejects ascribed group inferiority and takes an intersectional, anti-discrimination stance.

organic-representation.rationale: Inferred from commitment to individual citizenship and party-based democracy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; radical national regeneration is foreign to reformist liberalism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Mill and other liberal feminists rejected rule founded on personal authority rather than law and consent.

bound-labor.rationale: Mill compares women's subjection to slavery and demands freedom of occupation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Mill's emphasis on custom as untested bias gives it some purchase, yet liberal feminism relies on shared reason and evidence, unlike standpoint theory.

universal-morality.rationale: Liberal feminism rests on universal moral claims about equal worth and human rights, though critics say the universals were particulars.

single-common-good.rationale: Liberal pluralism accepts competing interests and women's claims as one of them.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not addressed in liberal feminist sources, and adherents have no shared view.

revive-national-language.rationale: Reviving a national language is unrelated to liberal feminism's documented programme, and adherents have no shared view.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; some social-democratic strands may agree but there is no stated position.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; NOW emphasises enforcing equal opportunity in public education, so mild opposition is inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed in the sources, and the movement's economic range from center-right to center-left leaves adherents split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Libertarian and neoliberal strands agree, social-democratic ones do not.

rule-by-example.rationale: Liberal feminism wants legal rights and enforcement, not reliance on rulers' virtue; Mill attacks reliance on unchecked power.

national-self-determination.rationale: The sources give no position on national self-determination; universalist rights liberalism pulls one way and no shared doctrine settles it.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from preference for rules-based international order.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Wollstonecraft and Mill grounded women's equality in reason and denied that custom or sentiment justifies subordination, though modern adherents include religious women.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; universalist rights framework suggests opposition.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between work-participation goals and concern for care burdens.

class-collaboration.rationale: Liberal feminism pursues pragmatic cross-class coalitions and partnership with men rather than opposed camps.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to reformist liberalism.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western fronts are not part of liberal feminism's concerns, and its universalist stance pulls against it, leaving no clear adherent view.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed; universalist rather than national class organisation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Mill argues that occupations should be open to all capable people regardless of sex, and NOW demands equal partnership.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to liberal economics.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The NOW statement states human rights are indivisible and links women's cause to civil rights.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Liberal feminism treats the state as a tool women can use to secure equality, unlike the Marxist view.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; center-left leanings suggest mild opposition.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; intersectional liberalism favours pluralism, though integration into mainstream is a theme.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in the sources and contrary to egalitarian liberalism.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; no stated position, though some feminists favour it for women's representation.

national-mission.rationale: A national mission to spread a form of government is not a liberal feminist theme, and adherents are divided between rights promotion and scepticism of it.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Liberal feminists hold that law and custom have systematically disadvantaged women, as Mill and NOW document, but see this as a barrier to remove rather than a total system.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Liberal feminism seeks to enter existing political institutions, not denounce them wholesale.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts the liberal feminist commitment to reproductive autonomy and equal moral worth.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from rule-of-law and rights liberalism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Liberal feminism calls for federal enforcement, childcare centres and retraining, which exceed a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts equal rights and indivisible human rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The NOW statement begins with women as human beings entitled to full development, and liberal feminism rests on equal respect for persons.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The question of settler states is not addressed in the sources, and adherents hold varied views, so neutral.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal legal status for women across personal-law systems is a liberal feminist goal, as Mill demanded one legal standard for marriage.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from liberal freedom of conscience.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal opposition to religiously motivated bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from secular rights framework; not stated.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred; a Leninist doctrine alien to liberal feminism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Liberal feminism grounds legitimate government in equal participation and consent, and fought for women's inclusion in that consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aim not addressed; inferred liberal economic leanings.

population-transfer.rationale: Contradicts the rights framework and equal human rights.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The libertarian absolute is not held by mainstream liberal feminism, though libertarian feminists do hold it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed; the struggle framing is not liberal feminist, though competition for open careers is valued.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Liberal feminists weigh free association against protecting democracy, and no source states a common position.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Mill describes wives' legal subjection as bondage, which fits domination language; republican wording is not standard for liberal feminism but adherents agree in substance.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred from commitment to constitutional liberal democracy and enforceable law.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine contrary to liberal pluralism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed; social-democratic strands agree while others do not.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is not addressed in liberal feminist sources, and adherents differ along ordinary left-right lines.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; liberal feminism locates disadvantage in institutions and law.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Intersectional, inclusive liberal feminism rejects this.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from favouring elections and equal candidacy.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Emergency price controls are not discussed in the sources, and the movement's mixed economic views leave adherents split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Incompatible with liberal democracy and free expression.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from inclusive rights outlook.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; liberal feminism favours individual representatives working across parties.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Not addressed; mild inference from liberal internationalism.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from parliamentary, legally constrained government.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed, and unrelated to the programme.

clerical-rule.rationale: Contradicts secular rights liberalism and women's equality.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist slogan alien to liberal feminism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Mill's liberalism opposes moral censorship; liberal feminism inherits this.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from constitutional limits on power.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are not addressed by liberal feminist sources and adherents have no common stance on them.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to the programme.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from modernising orientation.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is outside liberal feminism's documented concerns, so no adherent position can be stated.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Liberal feminism prizes women's education, as NOW demands equal educational opportunity.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Liberal feminists criticise practices that subordinate women yet respect pluralism; critics of liberal feminism target its universalism, so adherents split.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from center-left rights liberalism.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Education on sexuality and gender equality is a liberal feminist priority tied to reproductive autonomy and equal opportunity in schooling.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Liberal feminists lean against restriction on speech grounds, but NOW-linked feminists and others have supported limits, so adherents are divided.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is not addressed in the sources, and liberal feminists differ between pluralist support and common-language integration.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Liberal feminists worry that exemptions let religious institutions discriminate against women, as NOW targets discrimination in churches.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's On Liberty argument for eccentricity underlies his case against custom, and he attacks social pressure shaping women.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt is not discussed in the sources, and adherents' economic range from center-right to center-left leaves them divided.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonial economic transformation is not part of liberal feminism's programme, and adherents have no shared view.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting by assembly is not addressed in the sources and adherents have no shared preference.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from universalist human-rights commitments; not a stated demand.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of choosing a head of state is not a liberal feminist concern, and adherents hold no common view.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in the sources, and neoliberal and social-democratic strands would answer differently.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The sources do not address the justification of property; Mill's liberalism and social-democratic strands pull in different directions.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; mild inference from center-left leanings.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal internationalism.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from rights and consent principles.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not addressed; liberal feminism wants anti-discrimination law to bind churches, but not subordination.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The constitutional role of a head of state is not covered by the sources and adherents hold no shared view.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomy arrangements for regions are not addressed by liberal feminist sources, so no position is stated.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Mill rejects authority resting on custom and unchosen status, and liberal democracy treats rulers as accountable.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; center-left leanings suggest preference for progressive tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Wollstonecraft's and Mill's argument is that women's supposed nature is largely produced by education and circumstance.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is not part of liberal feminism's documented concerns, and adherents are indifferent or divided.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not addressed in the sources, and liberal feminism has no stated view on it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Liberal feminism relies on rule of law applied equally.

equal-parenting.rationale: Liberal feminists support shared parenting in principle but disagree about default presumptions in custody courts.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine foreign to the tradition.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; reformist liberalism favours compensated, legal means.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return claims are not discussed in liberal feminist sources, and adherents hold no shared view.

women-must-cover.rationale: Liberal feminism defends women's autonomy to choose how to live and dress, rejecting legal compulsion.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not addressed by the sources, and adherents differ along ordinary economic and national lines.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not part of the documented programme, and liberal feminists are wary of group claims that constrain women yet also pluralist, leaving them split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the strategy of winning equal rights within existing states.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist claim; liberal feminism emphasises law and ideas of equal rights.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; mild inference from regulating discriminatory and concentrated power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm bailouts are not addressed in the sources, and the movement's range from market to social-democratic views leaves it split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberal feminism depends on courts enforcing equal rights against majority prejudice, as the NOW statement demands.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Bringing women into the decision-making mainstream is a NOW aim, and liberal feminists tend to favour measures to secure equal representation, though some prefer merit-only access.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; autarky is foreign to liberal feminism.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; mild inference from center-left leanings.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to the programme.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Contrary to gradual reform within liberal democracy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Mill compares the subjection of women to birth-based exclusion and argues that no one should be barred by birth.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Liberal feminists back affirmative action, though some critics within it prefer class-based measures.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is outside liberal feminism's documented concerns, and adherents have no shared view.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Liberal feminism works within capitalism and assumes reform can succeed.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to the programme.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis not held by liberal feminism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Liberal feminism demands laws against discriminatory practices, as the NOW statement does by pressing enforcement of Title VII.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: NOW demands enforcement of constitutional guarantees, and liberal feminists look to entrenched rights and courts to secure equality.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The status of colonial-era treaties is not discussed in the sources, and adherents hold no shared view.

elective-rulers.rationale: Elective, accountable government with women's full participation is the liberal feminist standard.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from liberal constitutionalism; not a stated feminist theme.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not addressed; some feminists want courts to constrain parliaments.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; mild inference from liberal humanitarianism.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Liberal feminism rejects paternalistic protection that fosters dependence, which NOW explicitly opposes.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Liberal feminism is a participatory movement aiming at full public and political life.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: NOW protests false images of women in the media but liberal feminism does not accept the Frankfurt School thesis of pacification.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim; liberal feminism does not frame society as ruling-class hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim not held by liberal feminism.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations among communist parties are not a liberal feminist topic, so no adherent position can be stated.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from equal-rights principles.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is not addressed in the sources, and adherents hold no shared position on writing it into constitutions.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The comparison of fascism and communism is not addressed in liberal feminist sources, and adherents differ on it.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; Mill compares women's subjection to slavery and liberal feminism has abolitionist roots.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: NOW says men are harmed by half-equality and seeks partnership with men, but liberal feminism does not make men's disadvantage a programme.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Mainstream liberal feminism treats violence against women as the central concern, though it does not deny men's victimisation.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Liberal feminism holds universal equal rights apply everywhere, though critics call this universalism a particular.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Contrary to civilian liberal democratic government.

paid-care-work.rationale: Liberal feminists want childcare and recognition of care, as NOW and Nussbaum stress, but wages-for-housework is a socialist feminist demand.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; care obligations are debated by liberal feminists.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; merit access is welcome, but no view on exams specifically.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Mill demanded that the wife not be bound to bondage-like marriage and Stanton's work included divorce law reform.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from preference for representative democracy.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; women's longer lives and career breaks make adherents wary.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; foreign to the programme.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Liberal feminism has pressed for enforcement against structural employment discrimination, as NOW does with the pay gap and job segregation; the exact legal test is not stated.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism is not a theme of the sources; neoliberal strands tolerate it while social-democratic ones criticise it, so adherents split.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Liberal feminism applies Mill's anti-subjection logic to rule by one group over another, and the NOW statement treats human rights as indivisible.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from liberal concern with equal political voice; not a defining feminist issue.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from liberal support for open civil society and academic freedom.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Liberal feminism backs reproductive choice and childcare, not natalist state policy; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from liberal support for equal, open access to property and housing.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from reform within existing markets, with equal-opportunity law rather than job guarantees.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Liberal feminism works through law and the courts, so it accepts a general duty to obey while reforming it.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from liberal support for international human-rights intervention, as in CEDAW.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not a feminist issue and liberal feminists split on unions; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A liberal movement committed to equal rights rejects conspiracy claims against minorities.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The NOW Statement of Purpose seeks equal partnership in marriage, not its abolition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from liberal support for transparency and accountability.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; liberal feminists are generally indifferent or favour open trade.

informal-organisation.rationale: It works through legislatures, courts and a formal organisation such as NOW.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Liberal feminism draws on international human-rights law such as CEDAW; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Liberal feminism is secular-liberal and defines citizenship by equal rights, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Liberal feminism upholds the equal sovereignty of states and individuals and rejects ritual submission; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Mainstream liberal feminism supports redistribution across regions as part of equal citizenship; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Liberal feminism accepts private property and personal belongings and is not collectivist; inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Liberal feminism has no distinct view on communism; adherents are split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Liberal feminism sits within liberal democracy, which commonly accepts mixed public-private provision in publicly funded systems; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Liberal feminism is mostly neutral on religion and values freedom of belief; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Liberal feminism sits within the liberal tradition that credits capitalism with expanding opportunity; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Liberal feminism holds equality can be won through legal and political reform within the existing system, not by transforming it.

socialized-care.rationale: NOW proposed child-care centres and support so women can work, but not socialising all housework and childcare.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Liberal feminism does not address language purity and values openness; inferred from liberalism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Liberal rule-of-law thinking generally treats treaties as binding commitments; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Liberal feminism is individualist and works within existing institutions, not property-holding communes; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Liberal feminism's rights framework opposes ethnic engineering of regions; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Liberal feminism operates within liberal capitalism and mixed economies, not a third course; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Liberal feminism grounds claims in individual rights and equal respect, not in group ancestry or religious ties to land; inferred from that universalism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The sources do not discuss it, but a liberal-rights tradition would reject denial as false; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Liberal feminism's grounding in autonomy and equal respect, and the NOW call for equal rights, imply opposing criminal penalties for private adult conduct.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Liberal feminism works through legislatures, courts and open political participation within liberal democracy, so suppressing opposition contradicts its method.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Liberal feminism sits within liberal democracy's freedom of conscience and expression, and Mill argued against custom and authority as grounds for restraint.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Mill's and liberalism's equal-rights principles, though Mill himself accepted some imperial rule.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; a secular liberal movement would not endorse religious military obligations, inferred from its secular liberal framework.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to secular, representative government and change through legal reform rather than force.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Liberal feminism stresses equal access to representative institutions and public life more than direct participation, though it welcomes wider involvement; adherents are not clearly committed either way.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Liberal feminism targets legal and institutional sex discrimination as a separable barrier, and intersectional critiques are usually made against it.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from equal-rights and autonomy principles; the founding sources do not address it and contemporary liberal feminists are divided.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not a feminist issue and liberal feminists are split between autonomy arguments and concerns about pressure on vulnerable people.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Liberal feminism works within party and legislative politics where left and right matter, and its economics range across both; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation is a Marxist concept, and the scope excludes Marxist and socialist feminism; liberal feminists seek equal access to paid work rather than a critique of wage labour.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from liberal commitments to equal respect and non-discrimination by religion; not discussed in the sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Liberal feminism rests on liberal democracy and equal citizenship, in which authority comes from consent, and Mill attacked custom and inherited authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Liberal feminists split between neutrality of the state and individual freedom and women's autonomy in choosing dress; the sources do not settle it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Liberal feminism centres on enforcing anti-discrimination law through the courts, which the NOW program stresses, so keeping harassment claims out of court runs against its method.

social-market-economy.rationale: Its economics range from centre-right to centre-left, and a regulated market with social protections such as childcare and retraining fits the middle of that range.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; liberal democratic feminism accepts national defence and seeks women's equal place in it, inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from equal-opportunity principles, which oppose deliberately unequal starting positions, though some strands accept market-driven inequality.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; liberal democratic feminism is generally internationalist and aligned with liberal democracies, inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from the demand for equal opportunity by merit, which Mill set against inherited privilege and status by birth.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal feminism's working within market liberal democracy, which favours ordinary profit-making banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed, and its economics range from center-right to center-left, so adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: Its core claim is equal political rights regardless of sex, resting on universal citizenship rather than a wealth test.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist links between women and nature are treated as a separate feminist strand, so a liberal feminist is inferred to see the issues as separate.

reification.rationale: Inferred from its liberal, non-Marxist outlook; reification is a Marxist concept liberal feminism does not use.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from liberal commitment to press and assembly freedom as real rights; the hollow-rights critique is a socialist one.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: It works through legislatures and courts and enforcement of equal law, in line with liberal rule of law.

racial-franchise.rationale: The NOW Statement of Purpose demands equality and opposes discrimination and denial of rights on grounds of race as well as sex.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-democratic emphasis on women's equal participation in public life.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-democratic emphasis on accountable public institutions.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Mill demanded legal equality and freedom within marriage, which rules out state limits on whom adults may marry.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: NOW rejected discrimination and exclusion as contrary to equal rights and full participation.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not a stated liberal feminist position; inferred from its emphasis on women's equal voice in public life and deliberative, rights-based liberal democracy, so mild support.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Mill's argument that custom is no evidence of nature and from liberal feminism's push to update traditions that subordinate women; the sources do not address religious doctrine directly.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not a defining issue; liberal feminism is generally center-left on material inequality and worried about concentrated economic power, though market-liberal strands differ.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Liberal feminism's equal-rights principle extends to open service on equal terms; inferred, as the sources focus on sex equality.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Liberal feminism assumes liberal neutrality and freedom of conscience, so state promotion of atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: It works through law enforcement and the courts to secure rights, so abolishing police and prisons runs against its method.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; liberal individual-rights thinking favours majority rule with rights protections, but consociationalism is not rejected outright.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: NOW-style liberal feminism looks to public programmes such as childcare and enforced equal-opportunity law rather than charity; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; liberal reformers are divided on term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; it favours representative democracy and equal participation but has no stated view on delegable voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Unaddressed; mild agreement inferred from the mainstream liberal-democratic view that long-term public risks merit policy attention.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Its equality principle favours women's eligibility for all offices, though liberal feminism respects religious freedom and so does not seek to compel it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Mill's Subjection of Women attacks the husband's legal authority and the NOW Statement of Purpose calls for a truly equal partnership in marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Liberal feminism's emphasis on equal rights and inclusion fits extending local voting to long-term residents, though it is not a stated aim.

rent-control.rationale: Liberal feminism is split between market-oriented and welfare-oriented strands on housing regulation; it has no stated position.

abolish-ip.rationale: Liberal feminism accepts property and the market, including intellectual property; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Liberal feminism favours individual liberty and rejects drilled national-service youth movements; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Mainstream liberal-democratic feminists are inferred to oppose nuclear weapons on home territory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Liberal feminism has no stated position on foreign military bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Liberal feminism's rights framework is inferred to support formal recognition of mass atrocities.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Liberal feminism's economic views range from centre-right to centre-left; it is not clearly for or against this.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Liberal feminism's rights tradition recognises self-defence as legitimate; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Liberal feminism treats national identity as constructed and changing, not an unbroken inheritance; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Liberal feminism generally distinguishes biological sex from socially constructed gender, treating the sex-gender distinction as standard.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Liberal feminism organises around women as a shared group in seeking equal rights, so it does not reject the category.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Liberal feminism is secular-political and distrusts exalting the national dead as saints; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Liberal feminism treats politics as a matter of rights and reasoned reform, not a spiritual struggle; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Liberal feminism has no stated view on diaspora homelands.

culture-before-state.rationale: Liberal feminism pursues legal and political reform directly rather than waiting for cultural renewal; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Liberal feminists who engage with religion, such as in reform movements, favour inclusive God-language; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Liberal feminism judges traditions by their treatment of women's equality; inferred from its equal-rights core.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Liberal feminism's equal-rights principle rejects giving majority groups priority in economic life; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Liberal feminism is indifferent to the territorial organisation of peoples.

independent-unions.rationale: Liberal feminism backs workers' rights to organise as part of equal economic opportunity; the sources do not discuss union independence directly.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Liberal feminism works within liberal democracy and excludes Marxist and socialist feminism, so it does not make working-class rule the test of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Center-left liberal feminism supports public provision of services; inferred from NOW-style positions, and libertarian strands differ.

second-chamber.rationale: Liberal feminism is about equal rights under law and does not address legislative design.

municipal-property.rationale: Liberal feminism accepts private property and markets within liberal democracy, and does not call for community ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The tradition works through national legislatures and courts for uniform legal equality, not local assemblies; inferred.

family-wage.rationale: NOW and Mill reject treating women as dependants and press equal pay, so a wage set to support a worker's family assumes a male breadwinner model they oppose.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The tradition does not address drug approval.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Liberal feminism does not address ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; liberal feminists are divided between privacy and law-enforcement concerns.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between privacy and protection from online abuse.

person-over-state.rationale: Mill's individual liberty and equal rights for each person are core liberal feminist claims, as is each woman as an end in herself.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Liberal feminism is secular in method and neutral about spirituality; adherents differ.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Liberal feminism does not address regional autonomy.

racial-group-interests.rationale: NOW's statement seeks equality across race and sex under a common law, not separate racial organisation; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; liberal feminists would accept it as legitimate but treat it as outside their agenda.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; adherents are split.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Liberal feminism rests on universal individual rights and common citizenship rather than ethnic or linguistic nationhood; inferred from that universalism.

communal-electorates.rationale: Equal individual citizenship under common law is the core liberal-feminist model, so separate electorates by community are inferred to be rejected.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nothing in the tradition endorses plot narratives; its adherents would treat them as exaggerated. Inferred from its rights-based, reformist outlook.

free-public-college.rationale: NOW's 1966 statement demands equal access to education and training, so cost-free public college is inferred as welcome to most, though market-liberal strands would object.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Mainstream liberal feminists are inferred to accept market-based environmental tools alongside other policy; the tradition has no stated position.

future-generations.rationale: Liberal political philosophers such as Nussbaum and Okin work within a justice framework that extends to future persons; inferred, not stated in the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Liberal feminism stresses women's equal rationality and the same rights as men, in contrast to difference or care feminism, so it resists giving women's presumed distinct values extra weight.

arms-reduction.rationale: Reducing arms to a security minimum fits the mainstream liberal-internationalist outlook; inferred as the tradition has no stated position.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Open, accountable government is a liberal-democratic commitment; inferred as the sources do not discuss diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Liberal feminism sits within liberal democracy with economics from centre-right to centre-left, so state control of capital flows is inferred to be disfavoured.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from liberal-democratic reliance on the state's legal order and enforcement; not a feminist-specific issue.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: liberal feminism works within the law and wants women integrated into public institutions, including service, rather than orders refused.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: liberal feminism's economics range from centre-right to centre-left (s1), so adherents split on bargaining versus individual contracts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: centre-left liberal feminists favour supports that keep women in paid work, in line with NOW's retraining and childcare proposals (s4), though the right wing differs.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: no stance in the sources, and the centre-right and centre-left strands differ (s1).

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: Nussbaum-style global justice leans toward it, but the sources do not address it and the strands differ.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Liberal feminism works through legislatures, courts and enforcement of existing law to integrate women into the mainstream (s1, s4), so smashing the state is rejected.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: it seeks equal rights and opportunity within one liberal democratic framework, enforced through law, rather than varied community systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: not addressed in the sources and no distinctive liberal-feminist stance.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: liberal feminism grounds its claims in individual autonomy and equal respect (s2), not a sacred community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: it prizes equal access to education (s3, s4) and the centre-left strand would back relief; the right wing may not.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: a structural-exploitation framing belongs to radical and Marxist feminism, which this audit excludes (s1).

shared-human-nature.rationale: Liberal feminism grounds rights in shared human capacities for autonomy and equal respect (s2) and Mill rejected custom as proof of a different nature for women (s3); 'should not be redesigned' goes beyond the sources, so medium.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from centre-left liberal democracy; not addressed in the sources.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Liberal feminism is neutral on religion and defends freedom of conscience, taking no stance on whether religions share one truth (inferred).

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm policy is not a liberal feminist concern and its center-right and center-left strands differ (inferred).

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Liberal feminists are split on nuclear deterrence and the movement has no common line (inferred).

workers-own-party.rationale: Liberal feminism works through the existing parties and legislatures rather than separate class parties (inferred from its mainstream strategy).

ban-fgm.rationale: Liberal feminism grounds itself in autonomy and bodily integrity and presses legal protection of women, so it supports prohibiting FGM (implied by core principles).

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Mill and the NOW statement demand equal legal rights for women in property and marriage, which covers owning and inheriting land.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Liberal feminism has no position on language naming; nothing in its principles bears on it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Liberal feminism's center-left strand favours agency regulation of pollution, though the libertarian strand might prefer tort liability (inferred).

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Liberal feminism favours equal individual rights and sees customary authority as a source of women's subordination, as Mill did of custom (inferred).

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Liberal feminism prizes individual liberty and rights, so it resists putting any good above them by default, though it backs environmental policy (inferred).

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Liberal feminists generally favour judicial discretion and criticise mandatory minimums for disparate effects (inferred from liberal legalism).

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Liberal feminism has no stated view and adherents are split between integration support and language requirements (inferred).

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Liberal feminist organisations such as NOW work with the labour movement, so mandatory representation is not opposed; inferred, not stated in the sources.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the liberal feminist stress on equal political participation; ID rules are not discussed in the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Liberal feminism rests on liberal state neutrality among doctrines, which implies equal legal standing for religious interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from Okin and Nussbaum, who judge democracies by whether they secure equal rights and capabilities, not by elections alone.

premarital-sex.rationale: The NOW Statement of Purpose backs women's control over their sexual and reproductive lives and rejects the sexual double standard.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from liberal feminism's commitment to civil liberties and free expression; shutdowns are not discussed in the sources.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: liberal feminists lean towards targeted public services and childcare, and the sources do not discuss a negative income tax.

women-suffrage.rationale: Votes for women and equal political rights are the founding demand of the liberal feminist tradition, argued in Mill's Subjection of Women and the NOW Statement.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Liberal feminists are split: some criticise patriarchal religious norms (Okin) while many are religious and see faith as compatible with equality.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from liberal feminism's rejection of natural hierarchies and its opposition to race discrimination; not directly discussed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The NOW Statement calls for enforcement bodies and commissions to secure women's equality, so dedicated state machinery fits liberal feminism.

missingStatements.text: The law should require equal pay for equal work regardless of sex.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1966 NOW statement documents the pay gap and presses enforcement of Title VII against sex discrimination in employment.

missingStatements.text: Governments should fund public childcare so that parents can stay in paid work.
missingStatements.rationale: NOW proposed a nationwide network of child-care centres and retraining so women need not leave public life.
missingStatements.declined: Public childcare funding is a policy detail; paid-care-work is not the same question and this view is single-audit.

missingStatements.text: Married women should have the same legal rights to property, earnings and children as their husbands.
missingStatements.rationale: Mill criticised the wife's near-bondage in law, with her property and earnings passing to the husband, and demanded legal equality.

notes: Strands differ on markets (neoliberal and libertarian vs social-democratic), sex work and pornography, and abortion within some groups. Most non-gender answers are low-confidence inferences.
